name: MySQL 1.0
notes: Released to a limited group of four people, according to David Axmark and Michael Widenius.

name: MySQL 3.11.1
notes: The first public release, a binary distribution for Solaris.

name: MySQL 3.23
notes: MyISAM, replication and full-text search, and the table-handler layer that brought in InnoDB and BerkeleyDB as transactional engines.

name: MySQL 4.0
notes: Query cache, UNION, InnoDB in the standard server, and the embedded server library.

name: MySQL 4.1
notes: Subqueries, prepared statements, per-column character sets with Unicode, and spatial (GIS) types.

name: MySQL 5.0
notes: Stored procedures, triggers, views, cursors, INFORMATION_SCHEMA and XA transactions.

name: MySQL 6.0
notes: An alpha series built around the Falcon storage engine, cancelled in 2009. Its optimizer work came back in 5.5 and later, and Drizzle forked from its code.

name: MySQL 5.1
notes: Partitioning, row-based replication, the event scheduler and the plugin API. The biggest fork point on the chart: MariaDB, Percona Server 5.1, InfiniDB and the 6.x and 7.x Cluster lines all start here.

name: MySQL 5.2
notes: A short-lived development series, abandoned before GA.

name: MySQL 5.4
notes: Sun’s performance preview with InnoDB scalability patches. It was folded into 5.5 rather than shipped as GA.

name: MySQL 5.5
notes: InnoDB becomes the default storage engine; semi-synchronous replication and PERFORMANCE_SCHEMA. The first GA under Oracle.

name: MySQL 5.6
notes: GTID-based replication, online DDL, InnoDB full-text search, multi-threaded replicas and optimizer trace.

name: MySQL 5.7
notes: A native JSON type, generated columns, multi-source replication and the sys schema. Group Replication became GA during the 5.7 series.

name: MySQL 8.0
notes: A transactional data dictionary, window functions, common table expressions, roles and utf8mb4 by default. Numbering skipped from 5.7 to 8.0. End of life in April 2026.

name: MySQL 8.1
notes: The first Innovation release. From here Oracle ships quarterly Innovation releases between Long-Term Support releases.

name: MySQL 8.4
notes: The first Long-Term Support release under the new model.

name: MySQL 9.0
notes: A VECTOR data type, and JavaScript stored programs in Enterprise Edition.

name: MySQL 9.7
notes: The next Long-Term Support release after 8.4.

name: MySQL 26.7
notes: The newest MySQL entry on the source chart.

name: MySQL Cluster 7.2
notes: Rebased on the MySQL 5.5 server.

name: MySQL Cluster 7.3
notes: Rebased on MySQL 5.6.

name: MySQL Cluster 7.5
notes: Rebased on MySQL 5.7.

name: MySQL Cluster 7.6
notes: The last release before Cluster moved onto the 8.0 server; the chart shows it feeding into MySQL 8.0.

name: MySQL Cluster 8.0
notes: Cluster numbering aligns with the MySQL server from here on.

name: MySQL Cluster 8.1
notes: Released alongside MySQL 8.1.

name: MySQL Cluster 8.2
notes: Released alongside MySQL 8.2.

name: MySQL Cluster 8.3
notes: Released alongside MySQL 8.3.

name: MySQL Cluster 8.4
notes: Released alongside MySQL 8.4.

name: MySQL Cluster 9.0
notes: Released alongside MySQL 9.0.

name: MySQL Cluster 9.1
notes: Released alongside MySQL 9.1.

name: MySQL Cluster 9.2
notes: Released alongside MySQL 9.2.

name: MySQL Cluster 9.3
notes: Released alongside MySQL 9.3.

name: MySQL Cluster 9.4
notes: Released alongside MySQL 9.4.

name: MySQL Cluster 9.5
notes: Released alongside MySQL 9.5.

name: MySQL Cluster 9.6
notes: Released alongside MySQL 9.6.

name: MySQL Cluster 9.7
notes: Released alongside MySQL 9.7.

name: MySQL Cluster 26.7
notes: Released alongside MySQL 26.7.

name: RonDB 21.04
notes: The first RonDB release, based on MySQL Cluster 8.0.

name: RonDB 24.10
notes: Rebased on MySQL Cluster 8.4.

name: Percona Server 5.0
notes: Percona’s patched “highperf” builds of MySQL 5.0 (Percona was founded in 2006), where the Percona Server line begins.

name: Percona Server 5.1
notes: Introduced XtraDB, Percona’s enhanced InnoDB (announced December 2008 as a fork of the InnoDB plugin 1.0.2), which MariaDB then adopted as its default InnoDB. The “Percona Server” name was adopted during the 5.1 series in 2010.

name: Percona Server 5.5
notes: First stable release 5.5.11-20.2 on 28 April 2011. Took binary log group commit from MariaDB 5.3.

name: Percona Server 5.6
notes: First GA release 5.6.13-61.0 on 7 October 2013.

name: Percona Server 5.7
notes: First GA release 5.7.10-3 on 5 February 2016. Percona’s buffer-pool mutex split (MySQL bug #75534) was contributed back and landed in MySQL 8.0 as WL#8423.

name: Percona Server 8.0
notes: First GA release 8.0.13-3 on 21 December 2018. 8.0.46-37 (June 2026) was the last standard release; MySQL 8.0 is end of life, and 8.0 continues only as post-EOL builds.

name: Percona Server 8.1
notes: Percona’s first Innovation release, 8.1.0-1 on 27 November 2023.

name: Percona Server 8.2
notes: 8.2.0-1 on 5 February 2024.

name: Percona Server 8.3
notes: 8.3.0-1 on 16 April 2024, the last Percona Innovation release: Percona skipped all of MySQL 9.0–9.6.

name: Percona Server 8.4
notes: Tracks the MySQL 8.4 Long-Term Support release. First release 8.4.0-1 on 28 August 2024.

name: Percona Server 9.7
notes: Tracks the MySQL 9.7 Long-Term Support release. 9.7.0 was skipped; the first build is 9.7.1-1 on 5 August 2026.

name: Percona XtraDB Cluster 5.5
notes: The first GA release, 5.5.20, built on Percona Server 5.5.20 and the Galera library.

name: Percona XtraDB Cluster 5.6
notes: First GA release 5.6.15-25.2 on 30 January 2014, with Galera 3.

name: Percona XtraDB Cluster 5.7
notes: First GA release 5.7.14-26.17 on 29 September 2016. Added PXC Strict Mode and Galera instrumentation in Performance Schema.

name: Percona XtraDB Cluster 8.0
notes: First GA release 8.0.18-9.3 on 29 April 2020, with Galera 4. PXC 8.1–8.3 Innovation builds were never publicly released.

name: Percona XtraDB Cluster 8.4
notes: First release 8.4.2-2 on 11 December 2024, tracking MySQL 8.4 LTS.

name: Percona XtraDB Cluster 9.7
notes: First release 9.7.1-1, shipped in Percona Distribution for MySQL 9.7.1 on 10 September 2026. 9.7.0 was skipped.

name: GreatSQL 8.0
notes: Based on Percona Server 8.0.

name: GreatSQL 8.4
notes: Based on Percona Server 8.4.

name: TenDB 5.7
notes: Based on Percona Server 5.7.20.

name: VillageSQL 0.0.1
notes: The first release, based on MySQL 8.4.

name: VillageSQL 0.0.6
notes: Ships three server codebases: mysql-8.4 tracking MySQL 8.4, mysql-9.7 tracking MySQL 9.7, and percona-8.4 tracking Percona Server 8.4.

name: MariaDB 5.1
notes: The first MariaDB GA: MySQL 5.1 plus the Aria storage engine, with XtraDB as its InnoDB.

name: MariaDB 5.3
notes: A large optimizer release (subqueries and joins) and group commit, which Percona Server 5.5 took in.

name: MariaDB 5.5
notes: Merges MySQL 5.5.

name: MariaDB 10.0
notes: Numbering jumps to 10.0 to mark the split from MySQL 5.6: parallel and multi-source replication, and the CONNECT engine.

name: MariaDB 10.1
notes: Galera cluster built in, and data-at-rest encryption.

name: MariaDB 10.2
notes: Window functions and recursive CTEs. Takes InnoDB from MySQL 5.7, which replaces XtraDB as the default.

name: MariaDB 10.3
notes: System-versioned tables and an Oracle-compatible SQL mode. From 10.3.7 its InnoDB is no longer tied to a MySQL version.

name: MariaDB 10.5
notes: ColumnStore becomes part of MariaDB; S3 storage engine.

name: MariaDB 10.6
notes: Long-term support. Atomic DDL and JSON_TABLE.

name: MariaDB 10.7
notes: The first short-term release under MariaDB’s quarterly model.

name: MariaDB 10.11
notes: Long-term support.

name: MariaDB 11.0
notes: A new optimizer cost model.

name: MariaDB 11.4
notes: Long-term support.

name: MariaDB 11.7
notes: Vector search arrives.

name: MariaDB 11.8
notes: Long-term support, including vector search.

name: MariaDB 12.3
notes: Long-term support.

name: InfiniDB 1.5
notes: Calpont’s columnar engine, built on MySQL 5.1.

name: InfiniDB 4.0
notes: Relicensed under GPLv2.

name: InfiniDB 4.5
notes: The last InfiniDB release; InfiniDB Inc. closed later in 2014.

name: MariaDB ColumnStore 1.0
notes: MariaDB’s continuation of InfiniDB.

name: MariaDB ColumnStore 1.4
notes: Shipped only with MariaDB Enterprise 10.4 and no longer a separate fork; the code then merged into MariaDB.

name: Facebook MySQL 5.6
notes: The branch where MyRocks was built.

name: WebScaleSQL
notes: Announced as a shared MySQL 5.6 branch; Facebook’s 5.6 work fed into it heavily.

name: Drizzle 7.0
notes: The first GA release of Drizzle.

name: Drizzle 7.2
notes: Never reached GA; development stopped.
